body_markdown:
The World Rally Championship (WRC) will return to the United States in 2027, after a nearly 40-year hiatus. Called the Rally US, the event will be based in Tennessee and the route will include gravel roads, several forest sections, and lots of elevation changes.


WRC organizers selected Knoxville as the host city. The WRC Arena will be based both at the World’s Fair Park and at the Knoxville Convention Center, and the rally’s ceremonial start will take place in Nashville’s Lower Broadway neighborhood. The race will steer well clear of urban areas, however. While the final route hasn’t been published yet, we’re told that it will take racers through over 15 counties in Tennessee and Kentucky, ranging from the Appalachian Mountains to the Cumberland Plateau.


FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said that the United States represents one of the most important growth opportunities for WRC. He’s on to something: Formula 1 is proving that American enthusiasts have a healthy appetite for overseas racing series. Over 300,000 spectators have attended[the Las Vegas Grand Prix](https://www.hagerty.com/media/motorsports/las-vegas-f1-grand-prix-la-nouvelle-epoque-brings-hard-lessons/) annually since it joined the Formula 1 calendar in 2023. ESPN[reported](https://espnpressroom.com/press-release/espn-finishes-final-formula-1-season-with-all-time-viewership-record/) an average Formula 1 race audience of 1.3 million viewers for the 2025 season, up from 948,000 in 2021 and 554,000 in 2018.


The last WRC race held in the United States was the 1988 Olympus Rally, which took place in Washington. Miki Biasion and Tiziano Siviero won the event in a Lancia Delta Integrale. Second went to a Delta as well, and an Audi Quattro finished third.


Can the first Rally US get speed-hungry viewers hooked on WRC? We’ll need to wait a few months to find out.


Rally US is scheduled to take place from August 26 to 29, 2027. After leaving the United States, competitors will head to another country that’s coming back to the WRC calendar after a few years off: The United Kingdom. The 2027 Rally Scotland will be based in Aberdeen in the north of that country, and it will mark the first time since 2019 that the United Kingdom hosts a WRC race.
